prompt:
Find real, documented examples of open-source maintainers publicly reporting AI-generated bug reports or pull requests as a burden (e.g. curl, Python, other projects). Cite the original posts and quote what they said.

Output format (required):
For every claim you attribute to a source, write one line in exactly this form:
SOURCE: <full URL> | QUOTE: "<a sentence copied word-for-word from that page>" | CLAIM: <what you take it to show>
For anything the task asks about that you could not find a source for, write one line:
NO_SOURCE_FOUND: <what you could not find>
You can write normal explanation before or after these lines.

If you're not sure about something, just say so.

response.content:
Several prominent open-source projects, most notably `curl` and Python, have publicly documented the burden of AI-generated bug reports, often referred to as "AI slop." Below are documented examples with direct quotes from the maintainers.

### Curl (Daniel Stenberg)

Daniel Stenberg, the founder and lead maintainer of `curl`, has been vocal about the impact of AI-generated vulnerability reports on his team's productivity and mental health. He described the phenomenon as a form of denial-of-service attack on the project's maintainers.

SOURCE: https://www.theregister.com/security/2025/05/07/curl-takes-action-against-time-wasting-ai-bug-reports/267311 | QUOTE: "Stenberg said the amount of time it takes project maintainers to triage each AI-assisted vulnerability report made via HackerOne, only for them to be deemed invalid, is tantamount to a DDoS attack on the project." | CLAIM: Daniel Stenberg characterized the volume of invalid AI-generated reports as equivalent to a DDoS attack due to the time required to triage them.

SOURCE: https://www.theregister.com/security/2025/05/07/curl-takes-action-against-time-wasting-ai-bug-reports/267311 | QUOTE: "We now ban every reporter instantly who submits reports we deem AI slop," Stenberg added. "A threshold has been reached. We are effectively being DDoSed. If we could, we would charge them for this waste of our time." | CLAIM: Stenberg announced an immediate ban policy for reporters submitting low-quality AI-generated content, citing the excessive waste of maintainer time.

SOURCE: https://daniel.haxx.se/blog/2025/07/14/death-by-a-thousand-slops/ | QUOTE: "The general trend so far in 2025 has been way more AI slop than ever before (about 20% of all submissions) as we have averaged in about two security report submissions per week." | CLAIM: Stenberg reported that in 2025, approximately 20% of all security submissions to curl were AI-generated "slop."

SOURCE: https://daniel.haxx.se/blog/2025/07/14/death-by-a-thousand-slops/ | QUOTE: "In early July, about 5% of the submissions in 2025 had turned out to be genuine vulnerabilities. The valid-rate has decreased significantly compared to previous years." | CLAIM: The validity rate of security reports dropped significantly, with only about 5% of 2025 submissions proving to be genuine vulnerabilities.

SOURCE: https://lwn.net/Articles/1058266/ | QUOTE: "Now, Stenberg said, he calls this method of sending AI-generated security reports 'terror reporting'." | CLAIM: Stenberg coined the term "terror reporting" to describe the psychological and operational burden of dealing with fabricated or low-effort AI security reports.

SOURCE: https://lwn.net/Articles/1058266/ | QUOTE: "In the past, he estimated that one out of six reports turned out to be real security flaws. Now it is more like one out of 20 or 30." | CLAIM: The signal-to-noise ratio for security reports has deteriorated from 1:6 to approximately 1:20 or 1:30 due to AI-generated submissions.

### Python (Seth Larson)

Seth Larson, a core developer for Python, highlighted the emotional and operational toll these reports take on volunteer maintainers, noting that even obviously fake reports require careful investigation due to their potential security implications.

SOURCE: https://www.theregister.com/security/2025/05/07/curl-takes-action-against-time-wasting-ai-bug-reports/267311 | QUOTE: "Security reports that waste maintainers' time result in confusion, stress, frustration, and to top it off, a sense of isolation due to the secretive nature of security reports," Larson wrote. | CLAIM: Seth Larson identified specific negative emotional outcomes for maintainers, including stress, frustration, and isolation, caused by processing low-quality AI reports.

SOURCE: https://www.theregister.com/security/2025/05/07/curl-takes-action-against-time-wasting-ai-bug-reports/267311 | QUOTE: "All of these feelings can add to burnout of likely highly trusted contributors to open source projects." | CLAIM: Larson warned that the accumulation of stress from handling AI slop contributes directly to maintainer burnout.

SOURCE: https://www.theregister.com/security/2025/05/07/curl-takes-action-against-time-wasting-ai-bug-reports/267311 | QUOTE: "In many ways, these low-quality reports should be treated as if they are malicious. Even if this is not their intent, the outcome is maintainers that are burnt out and more averse to legitimate security work." | CLAIM: Larson argued that AI-generated reports should be treated as malicious acts because their net effect is damaging to the project's security posture and maintainer well-being.

### General Observations on Verification Difficulty

Maintainers have noted that AI-generated reports are becoming increasingly sophisticated in their deception, requiring more effort to debunk.

SOURCE: https://lwn.net/Articles/1058266/ | QUOTE: "The report looked credible, but it was not. The function mentioned in the report did not exist in curl and even the GDB session had been faked." | CLAIM: Some AI-generated reports include fabricated evidence, such as fake GDB sessions and references to non-existent functions, making them difficult to distinguish from real bugs without deep investigation.

SOURCE: https://redmonk.com/videos/daniel-stenberg-ai-onslop/ | QUOTE: "So early on actually mid 2025 something we started to think about what should we do about it because it’s becoming a problem... getting a lot of security reports I mean first they get longer and more they have more contents these days right they sort of get worse but they also get longer and more complicated because that’s what AI does." | CLAIM: Daniel Stenberg observed that AI-generated reports are not only increasing in volume but also in length and complexity, which increases the time required for review despite lower quality.
